title: Minimax Estimation of Two-Period Deterministic Clamp Policies in Longitudinal Studies
banked_reason: D0.5 kernel_substituted@thm:high-smoothness-frontier: accepted all-beta threshold-uniform matched frontier remains open for beta<=1/4; kill test has only nonmatching n^-1/10 to n^-1/18 bounds; independent validity gate confirms terminal kernel substitution.
gap_reasons: The matched result is uniform over threshold pairs only for beta greater than 1/4; at lower smoothness the moving stage-two face remains unresolved, while the all-smoothness theorem covers only fixed strictly positive thresholds.
proof_attempt_summary: Discovery derived the exact sequential recursion, a four-term lower bound, a matched threshold-uniform frontier for beta > 1/4, and an all-beta fixed-positive-threshold result. One bounded same-class fuzzy-likelihood attempt failed to close the beta = 1/8 moving-face gap; its proposed slower lower exponent was illegal under the likelihood and Holder restrictions. The accepted all-beta threshold-uniform kernel therefore remains open, and the delivered package was graded subfield below the fixed field floor.
tldr: An exact two-time deterministic clamp produces a retained-course term, two singular faces, and a joint corner. The note proves the causal bridge and exact recursion, the four-term same-class lower frontier for every fixed \(\beta>0\), the matching MSE and finite-sample honest-length frontier uniformly over both thresholds for \(\beta>1/4\), and the fixed-positive-threshold frontier for every \(\beta>0\). At low smoothness it proves a bracket, not an exact rate. In the kill test \(\beta=1/8\), \(\kappa_1=\kappa_2=0\), \(\delta_1=0\), and \(\delta_2=1/2\), the established bounds are \(c n^{-1/10}\leq\rho_{2,n}\leq C n^{-1/18}\), with the same orders for finite-sample honest expected length. A normalized signed full-likelihood construction has now been audited; after all Hellinger and Hölder regimes are enforced, it yields no separation beyond the existing \(n^{-1/10}\) face lower bound, so the exact low-smoothness rate remains open.
gap: Regular longitudinal modified-policy theory excludes deterministic clamps, the accepted one-time clamp frontier has only finite baseline strata, and the closest higher-order partial-mean result requires additional density structure while leaving minimax lower bounds and inference open.
fill: The project combines an exact sequential recursion, legal face-and-corner likelihood experiments, covariance-controlled estimation, bias-aware finite-sample intervals, and a multiresolution higher-order handle that either attains the oracle face scale or exposes and matches the missing nuisance mechanism.
